skill.name: omarchy-theming
skill.description: Create and manage Omarchy desktop themes, including colors.toml palettes, wallpaper folders, terminal colors, Hyprland colors, Waybar CSS, btop themes, and theme commands.
skill.summary: Build and validate Omarchy themes across desktop, terminal, browser, editor, and system UI configuration files.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and expected Omarchy configuration paths under ~/.config. One confirmed issue remains because the troubleshooting section asks users to run a privileged package installation command, and a semantic concern notes the trust risk of installing themes from arbitrary Git URLs.

remediation.issue: Privileged package installation command in troubleshooting guidance
remediation.suggestion: Avoid recommending sudo directly, or add clear guidance to verify the package source and use the system package manager only when the user approves.

remediation.issue: Remote theme installation from arbitrary Git URLs
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to install themes only from trusted repositories and inspect theme files before running install or update commands.

static_findings.snippet: Create themes for Omarchy by defining colors in `colors.toml`. Colors automatically propagate to all
2. Create `colors.toml` with all 22 required variables (see schema below)
1. **Always define all 22 color variables** in `colors.toml` - missing variables cause errors
2. **Use HEX format only** (`#RRGGBB`) - no RGB, HSL, or named colors
3. **Include `backgrounds/` directory** with at least one wallpaper image
4. **For light themes**, create empty `light.mode` file in theme directory

semantic_findings.title: Remote Theme Installation Requires Trust Review
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md documents omarchy-theme-install <git-url> and omarchy-theme-update commands. Installing or updating themes from arbitrary Git repositories can introduce untrusted theme files into the desktop configuration path.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command list directly includes remote theme install and update operations. The file does not show malicious intent, but remote theme sources create a real supply-chain trust boundary.

content.value_statement: Omarchy themes require many coordinated files across desktop applications. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through consistent theme creation, validation, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required Omarchy theme directory structure.
Defines the 22 required colors.toml color variables.
Shows how color variables map into CSS, TOML, RGB, and Hyprland formats.
Provides example dark and light theme palettes.
Documents Omarchy commands for applying, listing, installing, removing, and updating themes.
Covers optional theme files for Neovim, VS Code, btop, Chromium, and Hyprland.
limitations: It does not generate wallpaper images by itself.
It does not verify a theme visually without running Omarchy on the target desktop.
It assumes the user already has Omarchy and related theme commands installed.
Remote theme installation still requires user trust review.

use_cases.title: Create a new Omarchy theme
use_cases.description: Build a complete theme folder with required colors, wallpapers, and optional application files.

use_cases.title: Port an existing color palette
use_cases.description: Convert a known palette into the 22 required Omarchy color variables and related format variants.

use_cases.title: Fix a broken Omarchy theme
use_cases.description: Check missing variables, invalid color formats, missing backgrounds, and commands needed to regenerate theme files.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a new Omarchy theme named my-theme. Use a dark blue palette and list the files I need.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a palette
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this color palette into an Omarchy colors.toml plan with all required variables and explain each choice.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot theme output
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Omarchy theme structure and tell me why colors may not apply correctly across terminal, Waybar, and Hyprland.

prompt_templates.title: Design a complete theme package
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a full Omarchy theme with colors.toml, backgrounds, preview guidance, Neovim, VS Code, btop, Chromium, and light mode support.

output_examples.input: I want a dark Tokyo Night style Omarchy theme.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a complete theme plan with required color roles, folder structure, wallpaper placement, and application-specific notes.

output_examples.input: My light theme looks wrong in GTK and the browser.
output: Check that the light mode marker file exists.
Verify all required colors use standard hex format.

output_examples.input: How do I make the same accent color work in Hyprland and CSS?
output_examples.output: The skill explains which Omarchy variable forms use hex, stripped hex, and RGB decimal values for each target format.

best_practices: Define all 22 required colors before applying the theme.
Use standard hex colors for every colors.toml value.
Inspect remote theme repositories before installing or updating them.
anti_patterns: Do not omit the backgrounds directory when creating a theme.
Do not mix RGB, HSL, named colors, and hex values in colors.toml.
Do not run privileged package installation commands without user approval.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps create, organize, and troubleshoot Omarchy desktop themes and related application theme files.

faq.question: Does it create complete theme files?
faq.answer: It provides the structure, required variables, examples, and guidance needed to create complete theme files.

faq.question: Can it support light themes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the light mode marker file and the color choices needed for light themes.

faq.question: Which applications are covered?
faq.answer: It covers terminal themes, Hyprland, Waybar, btop, Neovim, VS Code, Chromium, and general Omarchy theme files.

faq.question: Does it install packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands, but users should approve and run any package installation themselves.

faq.question: Is remote theme installation safe?
faq.answer: Only install remote themes from trusted repositories after inspecting the files they add to your configuration.
